title: Monaco, Theming & Accessibility
objectives: Bundle Monaco offline with Vite workers
Define custom editor themes synced to app theming
Apply WCAG-minded practices to an IDE-like UI
body:
# Monaco Integration, Theming & A11y

## Offline bundling (no CDN!)

```ts
import EditorWorker from 'monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.worker?worker'
self.MonacoEnvironment = { getWorker: () => new EditorWorker() }
const monaco = await import('monaco-editor')     // lazy main lib
monaco.editor.defineTheme('rm-dark', { base: 'vs-dark', /* … */ })
```

Workers import statically so Vite emits chunks; the heavy library loads lazily
on first editor mount. Rust syntax ships built-in (basic-languages).
See `src/components/editor/CodeEditor.vue` for the production wiring.

## Themes follow the app, not the editor

One source of truth: settings store drives `<html class=dark>`; the editor
watches and calls `monaco.editor.setTheme(currentTheme())`. Define BOTH rm-dark
and rm-light at startup — never fetch themes remotely.

## Accessibility checklist for workbenches

- Keyboard-first: every action reachable; Ctrl+Enter run, Ctrl+S save (this
  app wires them via `useShortcuts` AND inside Monaco's command API).
- Focus visibility: `focus-visible` rings everywhere (see `.btn`).
- Landmarks & labels: `role="region"`, `aria-label` on editor/output panes.
- Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 both themes; high-contrast mode toggle for extra headroom.
- Motion: honor `prefers-reduced-motion`; provide manual override.

Screen-reader users should hear structure (headings, lists), not just code.
